chapter: Cee Pee Johnson, Hampton and the Navy band
title: Leaving for Hampton with brother Ernie; closeness to Ernie
summary: Royal, Ernie and Jack McVea left Johnson for Hampton's band, partly to give his brother exposure.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: How long did you work at the Rump Boogie? (inaudible)?

I worked with that band, '39 and into '40 until Lionel Hampton got his band. That's how Lionel got half his band out of that band. My brother Ernie and Jack McVea and I, we left the band and went into Lionel's band, see. So that's how that worked out.
So, when you joined Lionel Hampton, it was the first time that you were on the road since you were a child, is that right?
And what made you decide that you wanted to go out and travel?

Oh, just another little change. My brother was blossoming out as a first-class trumpet player at the time and I kind of thought it would be good for him to get a little exposure, get out, and we were very close, my brother and I, although there was eight years difference in our age. They used to call us the Corsicans, because we were always together, my brother and I. So, it was a lot of fun. We roomed together and we were always together and I was able to help him to become a young man and sort of act like a father to him, because he was hardly a teenager when my father died,
so he always looked up to me, so we had a chance to go out and be together and have some fun. So, we did.
